correctness.rationale: PASS: The fixed-level conic has k=q−χ(−1) even points. Nonzero conic cannot contain an affine line, yielding at most two circle intersections and a unique center for any common triple. Antipodal pairs have exactly one covering center; all other covered pairs have two. Consequently a shattered triple is precisely a concyclic nonantipodal triple; center incidences produce coefficients q²k²/4 and q²k(k−2)(k−4)/6; the triple obstruction bounds VC dimension by 3 and q=3,5 have no such triples. Verified finite traces for q=3,5,7, t=1,2 independently; unrestricted proof is geometric, not finite enumeration.
